items.title: RFC: alternatives to static build
items.body:
During the BPF Microconference at LPC, we got feedback that installing llvm/clang/libbpfcc in production servers just to use `bpftrace` would be overkill and sometimes unfeasible. An alternative would be linking to those dependencies statically, but most distributions don't provide the static library `libclang.a` on their libclang packages.

I started to think about alternatives to a static build, and two ideas came up:

## Have an option to compile a `.bt` file into an executable

In this approach, we would add a new option to `bpftrace` (let's say, `-o`), which instead of attaching to the probes we provided, would build an executable binary with our bpftrace program. We could then send this binary to a given server without having to install llvm/clang libraries there.

Downsides would be:

  - bpftrace would get more complex
  - I think we would still need libbpfcc installed on the server to attach to probes

## Compile a `.bt` file into an intermediate format, and run with a minimal bpftrace binary

Similar to the previous idea, but instead of creating an executable binary we would have an intermediate format with our probes as well as BPF programs for each probe. We could then use a minimal bpftrace binary (not linked against llvm/clang) to run this intermediate file.

On the upside, I think this would be more maintainable than the previous approach (internally we could also use the intermediate format). Downsides are the same as the previous approach.

---

I still think it's worth getting our static builds to work though, but if we can't do that reliably, we could start investigating those alternatives.

items.title: Switch development to llvm12
items.body:
As @Birch-san  raised in https://github.com/iovisor/bpftrace/discussions/1785 and https://github.com/iovisor/bpftrace/discussions/1782 our development proces is a bit annoying. 

With the release of LLVM12 I think its time to update our dev setup to LLVM12 only. Most distros have already moved away from llvm7 and 8-11 have the stack reuse bug so 12 seems like our best option.

I don't think we really need to test all these versions, our codegen is still pretty much the same between all versions. We might have a API rename, but no completely different logic.

That would mean our codegen and codegen validator tests would be LLVM 12 only. Support for all other versions can be dropped (just don't run the tests).

It's a bit of churn but afterwards we can ignore it again for 1.5/2y (hopefully)

@danobi @Birch-san @olsajiri @viktormalik  thoughts?

items.title: Update to Alpine 3.11 and BCC 0.12 for static builds
items.body:
This picks up where #867 and #917 left off and builds on their insights. The versions of Alpine and bcc that we're currently using are a bit old. A static package for bcc is now available in Alpine's `edge` repository, and it should significantly reduce our CI build times by avoiding an expensive compilation step.

For unclear reasons, the `ast` build target is including `-Wl,-Bdynamic /usr/lib/llvm8/lib/libLLVM-8.so` in the link step, which causes the static initialization failure and segfault noted [here](https://github.com/iovisor/bpftrace/pull/867#issuecomment-537624591). The problem seems to stem from `clang_libs` [0], but I spent a couple hours experimenting with cmake options and couldn't find a solution. I've left the sed hack from #867 in place to handle this for now.

Unfortunately the header parsing crashes noted in #266 are still happening with llvm8 and a newer BCC. A few of the unit and runtime tests are failing with similar errors for me locally when I use the static build. Seems like more evidence that it's an issue specific to musl.

FWIW, I feel like the approach outlined in #1041 is better for the long term, but maybe this can improve CI in the meantime.

Thanks to @sezuan, @danobi, and others for the earlier work on this.

-------

[0] You can "box in" the link options in the build output using something like this -- start-group and end-group can be any valid flag -- which suggested to me that `clang_libs` is involved in the incorrect linking:

```
target_link_libraries(ast -Wl,--start-group ${clang_libs} -Wl,--end-group)
```

libLLVM-8.so will appear at the end of the group.
